title: Ang 490–507: the Gurus in Gujri
hook: Guru Amar Das, Guru Ram Das and Guru Arjan
tomorrow: how does an elephant fit through a gate smaller than a seed?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Gujri begins: the Name as sandalwood, the mind as the grinding stone, good deeds as the saffron. Today the stone gets real.

There's a kind of late-night planning that isn't planning at all: the same worry run through your head on a loop, the numbers that won't add up no matter how many times you add them. On ang 495, Guru Arjan speaks straight to that mind. Why scheme and fret, he asks? And then he points at a rock. Inside the stone there are living creatures, and someone has already set their food in front of them.
screen: `THE LOOP AT NIGHT.` → `WHY SCHEME AND FRET?` → `FOOD INSIDE THE ROCK.`

segments.voice: These pages of Gujri belong to the Gurus, in order: Guru Amar Das, then Guru Ram Das, then Guru Arjan. And the hymn on ang 495 is the one to hold. In paraphrase: O mind, why do you plot and worry, when the Lord himself is busy caring for you? In rocks and stones he made living things, and set their food before them. Their rijak, their daily food, is already there. Then a bird flies far away, leaving her young behind. Who feeds them? Who teaches them to peck? Notice what the hymn is aimed at. Not work. Not effort. The word is the scheming, the anxious circling, the mind running the same numbers again at night. The picture answers it with something you can hold: a stone, solid, cold, and alive inside. Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight. This hymn, and one by Guru Ram Das from these same Gujri pages, are also part of Rehras, the prayer Sikhs say in the evening. So the hymn about the night worry is said as the day closes, just when the loop tends to start. The Gurus in Gujri hand you a rock, and say: something is already looking after what's inside it.
screen: `THREE GURUS, IN ORDER.` · `WHY SCHEME, O MIND?` · `FOOD SET OUT INSIDE THE ROCK.` · `ALSO SAID IN THE EVENING PRAYER.` · then, large: `GURUS IN GUJRI.`

segments.voice: Pick up a stone, a pebble, or anything solid and heavy enough to feel. Hold it in a closed hand for the sit and notice its weight, its cool, its edges. Each time the planning loop starts up, loosen your grip on the stone a little; afterward, if you'd like, read the hymn on ang 495.
Ang 490. Where the Gurus' hymns in Gujri begin: Guru Amar Das, Guru Ram Das, then Guru Arjan, and the rock with food inside it.
Gurus in Gujri: three voices, and a rock with its food already inside. Set it down gently tonight.

howItsDone: Sikhs say Rehras Sahib in the evening; it includes Gujri hymns by Guru Ram Das and Guru Arjan, among them the hymn asking the mind why it schemes and frets.

chat.says: up at 2am redoing our langar budget again. barely any money. how do ppl not panic
options: Plan once in daylight, then drop the loop; even a creature in a rock gets fed.
Stop planning at all; the hymn says effort means you don't trust God.
Keep going until it's perfect; the worry is how you show you care.
chat.meaning: Guru Arjan asks why the mind schemes and frets, when food is set out even for creatures in rocks. The target is the anxious loop, not the work.
